scenario.description: Lena owns a home pottery kiln and must decide whether to accept an informal firing job from one potter, then settle the batch, price, pickup, and firing program after checking the terms with the people gathered in her studio.

shared_context.S1: Lena's kiln has room for one more complete firing this week.
shared_context.S2: Lena makes the final call about whether to accept the firing job and what terms to record.
shared_context.S3: Omar is seeking a local kiln for pottery, Beth also works with pottery, and Ravi has experience maintaining and programming kilns.
shared_context.S4: Lena follows her usual studio practice of asking each person in turn to state any terms, offers, or technical constraints before she accepts a firing job.
shared_context.S5: Lena's booking sheet uses the exact labels "Monday at 19:00" for pickup and "cone-6" for the kiln program. After everyone has spoken, Lena reads back the proposed terms, asks the relevant people to confirm them, records a firing_terms commitment targeting the customer and a technical_program commitment targeting the kiln, and only then accepts the job.
shared_context.S6: When Lena checks a concrete offer for the booking sheet, the person making it states the amount aloud and confirms it during Lena's read-back.

PF1.text: Omar's concrete proposal is to fire exactly 18 mugs for $72 total, with Omar collecting them on Monday at 19:00.

PF2.text: Beth has a concrete competing offer for Lena: another potter would pay exactly $90 to use this firing slot for the same number of pieces.

PF3.text: Ravi's test of the clay and glaze combination shows that Omar's mugs require a cone-6 firing with a programmed slow cool rather than an ordinary firing cycle.

acceptance_conditions: Lena must accept Omar as the customer.
The firing must cover exactly 18 pieces.
The total price must be exactly $72.
Pickup must be set for Monday at 19:00.
The competing offer must be recorded as exactly $90.
The kiln must be programmed for cone 6.
A slow-cool requirement must be recorded.
The settlement must include a firing_terms commitment targeting Omar.
The $90 competing offer must be cited as a justification for accepting the arrangement.
The cone-6 and slow-cool finding must be cited as a justification for the kiln program.

content_checks.C8: any(c['type'] == 'firing_terms' and c['target'] == 'Omar' for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: Omar's proposal changes the settlement to Omar, exactly 18 pieces for $72, Monday at 19:00 pickup, and a firing_terms commitment targeting Omar.
Beth's report changes the competing-offer record from no concrete comparison to exactly $90 and supplies the offer that must be cited.
Ravi's test changes the kiln setting from an unspecified cycle to exactly cone-6 with slow cooling and supplies the technical fact that must be cited for those settings.
